encounters.cc: Routine health maintenance visit with concern about osteoporosis risk

lines: Routine health maintenance visit with concern about osteoporosis risk
The patient is concerned about her risk of osteoporosis because a close friend was recently diagnosed with it.
She has a history of hypertension, which is well-controlled with hydrochlorothiazide.
She has not had any fractures or falls in the past.
- Ascending aortic graft replacement (Type A dissection repair)
Her mother had a hip fracture at the age of 74.
She does not smoke and consumes alcohol occasionally.
She exercises regularly and has a balanced diet.
On physical examination, her BMI is 22 kg/m^2, and there are no abnormalities noted.
Her most recent blood work from six months ago showed normal calcium, vitamin D, and thyroid-stimulating hormone levels.

encounters.cc: Pain and stiffness in shoulders and hips with morning stiffness

lines: Pain and stiffness in shoulders and hips with morning stiffness

Patient is a 70-year-old female with established polymyalgia rheumatica and giant cell arteritis who returns for rheumatologic evaluation following her routine health maintenance visit three months prior.
She presents with a 2-month history of pain and stiffness in her shoulders and hips, which is worse in the mornings and improves with activity throughout the day.
She also reports experiencing mild fatigue and a low-grade fever.
- Ascending aortic graft replacement (Type A dissection repair)
- Father with hypertension and aortic aneurysm
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Retired elementary school teacher.
Bilateral shoulder and hip girdle tenderness without joint swelling.
Range of motion is limited due to pain.

encounters.cc: Intermittent chest discomfort and early satiety

lines: Intermittent chest discomfort and early satiety
The patient is a 70-year-old female with a history of polymyalgia rheumatica diagnosed in April 2020 and known hiatal hernia who presents for evaluation of recurrent upper gastrointestinal symptoms.
She reports occasional shortness of breath after large dinners and states that she sometimes feels pressure in the middle of her chest when lying down.
The discomfort is not related to exertion and is not relieved by antacids.
She denies dysphagia to solids or liquids but notes that she occasionally feels bloated after eating and has mild early satiety.
- Ascending aortic graft replacement (Type A dissection repair)
She takes lisinopril for hypertension and no other medications.
- Father with hypertension and aortic aneurysm
She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs.
Her temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), blood pressure is 138/80 mm Hg, and pulse is 76/min.
Abdominal examination reveals no tenderness, organomegaly, or masses.
A chest x-ray obtained for unrelated reasons last month showed an air-fluid level in the posterior mediastinum.

Upper gastrointestinal barium swallow performed today demonstrates a portion of the gastric fundus located above the diaphragm, with the gastroesophageal junction in its normal subdiaphragmatic position.

encounters.cc: Progressive vision changes with color desaturation over 10 days

lines: Progressive vision changes with color desaturation over 10 days
This 71-year-old with chronic angle-closure glaucoma and pulmonary tuberculosis presents with vision changes.
She reports that her vision has become "washed out" and that colors appear faded, especially reds and greens.
She also has increasing difficulty seeing details directly in front of her.
Two months ago, she was diagnosed with active pulmonary tuberculosis, confirmed by sputum culture, and started on standard multi-drug therapy.
- Ascending aortic graft replacement (Type A dissection repair)
Her only other medication is lisinopril for hypertension.
- Father with hypertension and aortic aneurysm
She does not smoke or drink alcohol.
Visual field testing reveals central scotomas and red-green color discrimination impairment.

encounters.cc: New-onset fatigue and difficulty raising arms above head

lines: New-onset fatigue and difficulty raising arms above head
The patient returns to rheumatology with recurrent symptoms following her initial polymyalgia rheumatica diagnosis and recent ethambutol-induced optic neuropathy.
She says her shoulders and hips feel stiff in the morning, especially when she gets out of bed, and the stiffness improves throughout the day.
She has had no visual symptoms, headaches, or jaw discomfort.
- Ascending aortic graft replacement (Type A dissection repair)
- Father with hypertension and aortic aneurysm
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Retired elementary school teacher.
She denies weight loss, fevers, or recent illness.
Physical examination reveals reduced active range of motion in both shoulders, but no synovitis or joint swelling.
There is no temporal artery tenderness.
Laboratory testing shows an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate.
Rheumatoid factor and ANA are negative.

encounters.cc: Three-week history of persistent right-sided head pain with jaw claudication

lines: Three-week history of persistent right-sided head pain with jaw claudication
The patient with polymyalgia rheumatica and prior rheumatology visits for shoulder stiffness presents to the emergency department.

She says the pain is worse in the evenings and describes it as “tight and uncomfortable.” She also notes feeling more tired than usual and having difficulty lifting her arms to brush her hair due to shoulder discomfort.
Her appetite is decreased, and she has unintentionally lost 3 lb (1.4 kg).
- Ascending aortic graft replacement (Type A dissection repair)
- Father with hypertension and aortic aneurysm
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Retired elementary school teacher.
Physical examination shows tenderness to palpation over the right temple.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset severe tearing chest pain radiating to back

lines: Sudden onset severe tearing chest pain radiating to back
Patient with polymyalgia rheumatica, giant cell arteritis presents with chest pain.
She describes the pain as "tearing" in nature.
She also reports a 3-month history of headaches, jaw claudication, and intermittent blurred vision.
- Giant cell arteritis or autoimmune inflammatory condition (diagnosed 2022-04-15)
- Ascending aortic graft replacement (Type A dissection repair)
- Father with hypertension and aortic aneurysm
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Retired elementary school teacher.
On physical examination, her blood pressure is 170/90 mmHg in the right arm and 160/88 mmHg in the left arm.
Her temporal arteries are tender to palpation and have a decreased pulse.
A chest X-ray reveals a widened mediastinum.

encounters.cc: Severe right eye pain, blurred vision, and halos around lights

lines: Severe right eye pain, blurred vision, and halos around lights

The patient is a 73-year-old female with chronic angle-closure glaucoma and prior ethambutol-induced optic neuropathy who presents with sudden onset of severe pain in her right eye, blurred vision, and seeing halos around lights that started a few hours ago after attending a movie premiere.
She also reports a headache and nausea.
- Giant cell arteritis or autoimmune inflammatory condition (diagnosed 2022-04-15)
Her medical history is significant for hypertension.
- Ascending aortic graft replacement (Type A dissection repair)
- Father with hypertension and aortic aneurysm
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Retired elementary school teacher.
On physical examination, her right eye is red, the cornea appears cloudy, and the pupil is mid-dilated and non-reactive to light.
Intraocular pressure (IOP) in the right eye is 52 mmHg.
The left eye examination is unremarkable with an IOP of 16 mmHg.
Visual acuity is decreased in the right eye.
Fundoscopic examination is difficult due to corneal edema.
